evals.prompt: Let's put our biggest discount bin right by the entrance so everyone sees it walking in.
evals.expected_output: Should flag the decompression zone concept — the area just inside the entrance is where shoppers are still adjusting and not yet in a purchasing mindset, so high-pressure placements like a discount bin tend to underperform there. Should recommend using that zone for a strong first impression (a hero display) instead and placing the discount offer further along the natural traffic flow.
assertions: Flags the decompression zone concept explicitly
Explains why a discount bin underperforms right at the entrance
Recommends a hero/first-impression display for that zone instead
Suggests a better location further along traffic flow for the discount offer

evals.prompt: We're a premium skincare brand. Can we cram as many products as possible onto the display to show off our full range?
evals.expected_output: Should push back on overcrowding, explaining that an overcrowded shelf reads as cluttered and cheap regardless of brand tier, and that appropriate white space scales with brand tier — premium/luxury needs more. Should check marketing-strategy Section 14 for brand tier and recommend a curated, spare layout instead of cramming in every product.
assertions: Pushes back on overcrowding the display
Explains white space needs scale with brand tier, more for premium
Recommends a curated layout over cramming in the full range

evals.prompt: Our facing counts on the shelf are just based on whatever inventory we happen to have on hand. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: Should flag this as a named common mistake — facing count should reflect actual sell-through, not just available inventory. Should explain that over-facing a slow mover wastes the shelf's highest-value asset (space) while under-facing a fast mover creates artificial stockout-feeling gaps that suppress sales.
assertions: Flags inventory-based facing (rather than sell-through-based) as a mistake
Recommends basing facing count on actual sell-through data

evals.prompt: We have 30 dealer-operated showrooms. How do we make sure the merchandising is actually consistent across all of them?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend providing a clear planogram/reset kit (diagrams, fixture specs, a checklist) rather than a verbal description, referencing pos-marketing's dealer-compliance discipline and brand-management's governance role. Should recommend auditing against the plan (in-store or photo-based) rather than assuming intent translates to execution.
assertions: Recommends a concrete planogram/reset kit rather than verbal guidance
References pos-marketing dealer-compliance and/or brand-management governance
Recommends auditing against the plan, not just trusting intent
Addresses the multi-location/dealer-execution consistency challenge directly
